config.name: round12_reference_consistency_features
config.question: Does consistency with other labeled references make support evidence more useful without deleting rare or disputed examples?
config.reference_status: context_evidence is an adaptively chosen exploratory anchor, not promoted
config.scope: original permitted support/training labels; no released targets
config.feature_construction_fits: 8 reference-only kNN quality graphs plus 8 shuffled-label statistics; no encoder or classifier fits here
config.promotion_gate: Primary >= +0.003 macro AUC against every specified comparator, simultaneous lows >0, no per-policy regression, ranked-pooled nondecrease vs raw Qwen. Exploration only.

config.name: round9_behavior_support_features
config.reference_status: Round 7 pinned; six Round 6 readouts reused without refitting.
config.selection: No validation-led feature selection or hyperparameter search.
config.pooling: Original 234/647 cohorts; same-rule references and group cross-fitting.

limitations: Exploratory adaptive development on the same 881 queries, not a fresh holdout or Kaggle score.
The context_evidence anchor is held fixed, selected after Round 9, and was never promoted.
New reference features are text-group cross-fitted. The inherited adapted answer score is in-sample on support labels.
Cross-fitting the new features cannot repair that inherited answer-score limitation.
Simultaneous intervals cover this round, not the full adaptive project history.
Both new designs are fixed before either run; no companion-round result is read.
Neighbor disagreement is not proof of a wrong label. No supplied label is edited or removed.
This is not Confident Learning or its noise-identification algorithm. The paper motivates label-quality awareness only.
Prior conflict dropping/soft-label experiments are distinct: original labels and training weights stay fixed.
Reliability is constructed anew inside each reference crossfit pool; held query labels never enter it.
